_doc: L4 GROWTH-CASE parameters. The corridor engine (atom.py/aggregate.py) produces the conservative FLOOR: 10% capture of TODAY's crossing demand, existing corridors, N30 only, transport-fare only. This layer turns that floor into the TAM/SAM/SOM ladder a super-app partner reads. EVERY rung is one multiplication off the model's own M_today (= sourced market_rev / capture_rate), so the prize stays traceable back to grounded demand. NULL-beats-guess still applies: greenfield is OFF by default; all multipliers are modeled (T4/T5) and reported as low/mid/high BANDS, never single points.

_whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
_whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
_whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

ladder._doc: Three rungs. SOM = published floor (unchanged). SAM = Navier transport revenue once the network matures (induced demand + capture ramp). TAM = total journey GMV across the induced crossing market on serviceable corridors.

som_capture_rate._doc: FLOOR capture used in the published model. New-entrant share of today's crossing pool. Locked in vessel-constants.json; mirrored here for the ladder.

induced_demand._doc: k_induced — how much the addressable crossing market GROWS because the product is transformational (2-3x faster, quiet, zero-emission, on-demand). A miserable 90-min ferry becoming a 25-min premium hop creates trips that don't happen today (day-trips, commutes, spontaneous crossings). Applied to the demand POOL.
induced_demand._precedent: Ride-hail grew urban for-hire-vehicle trips ~2-3x in mature markets (Uber/Lyft). Tempered DOWN here: island crossings still need a destination reason, so more constrained than urban rides. Bands sit below the urban ride-hail precedent on purpose.

mature_capture_rate._doc: c_mature — Navier's corridor share once it is the established premium default (vs the 0.10 new-entrant floor). On a corridor where Navier is clearly the best option, mature share is well above 10%.
mature_capture_rate._precedent: Category-leading mobility products routinely hold 20-40% corridor/market share at maturity. Floor stays 0.10 (SOM); this is the matured network.

journey_gmv_multiple._doc: m_attach — journey GMV as a multiple of the transport fare. Transport (the ferry seat) is only a slice of the island-journey wallet; the rest is food, activities/experiences, accommodation share, retail, ads, and parcel/logistics — all monetizable through a super-app.
journey_gmv_multiple._precedent: Transport is typically ~25-35% of a leisure day-trip / island-journey wallet, implying journey GMV ~= 3x the transport fare. Conservative vs full multi-day trip spend (we scope to the journey, not the whole holiday).

platform_take_rate._doc: Partner (Grab) blended commission on journey GMV across mobility + food + bookings + ads. Used only for the derived 'partner platform revenue' line.
platform_take_rate._precedent: Super-app blended take rates run ~18-22% across mobility/delivery/ads. 0.18 used as a conservative blended point.

greenfield_corridor_factor._doc: g_greenfield — WIDTH lever. Prefer PER-PARTNER census at finance/recal/greenfield-census/<partner>.json (finance/model/greenfield_census.py). Formula: g = 1 + (N_greenfield/N_sourced)*alpha_density, with tail softening when count_ratio > Grab ref 9.7. growth.py auto-loads partner census when present. Legacy band below is Grab SEA historical ONLY — do not use as a global assumption.

alpha_density._doc: avg greenfield corridor demand / avg sourced corridor demand. Sourced = cherry-picked best; greenfield thinner.

_census._note: LEGACY Grab SEA: tier1+tier2; local micro excluded. Rebuild: python3 finance/model/greenfield_census.py --all && python3 finance/rebuild_all_from_greenfield_census.py

vessel_roadmap_note._doc: Not a multiplier in this layer (kept honest). The N35 Shuttle (12-15 pax, 2027) roughly halves payback / ~doubles per-boat throughput vs the modeled 8-seat N30. Larger hulls multiply further. The entire ladder is computed on the WEAKEST boat we will ever run; treat N35+ as additional upside not yet priced in.
